html:
The Central Asia to China gas pipeline carries natural gas from Turkmenistan through Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan into Xinjiang in China. Its first line opened in December 2009.

Before it, almost all Turkmen gas had to flow north through Soviet era pipes to Russia, which set the price. In 2009 an explosion on the Russian line and a price dispute cut Turkmen exports badly. The new pipeline, paid for largely by China, ended Russia's hold. In China it joins the West-East Gas Pipeline, so gas can travel some 7,000 kilometres to Shanghai.

Three parallel lines now run, and more than half of Turkmenistan's gas exports go to China. The project was a sign of China's growing pull in Central Asia, a few years before Xi Jinping announced the Belt and Road Initiative in 2013 in a speech at Nazarbayev University in Astana. It is a modern partner to older energy routes such as the Caspian Pipeline Consortium.
sum: The Central Asia to China gas pipeline carries natural gas from Turkmenistan through Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan into Xinjiang in China. Its first line opened in December 2009.
